featured_reviews.review_text:
HIGHLIGHT - If you have been to Hyderabad's version, you will likely find this visit a complete letdown.

My recent visit to Mumbai Film City was far from what I had hoped. To start, the nearest metro station is Aarey, it is about 4 km away. From there, take an auto (no more than ₹150) straight to the official ticket counter. Be cautious, several individuals may try to sell you tickets along the way at inflated prices. Avoid them, as they are scammers.

After a long wait, we were taken inside the premises by an AC bus. Unfortunately, the experience was underwhelming from the beginning. Compared to Hyderabad's Film City, this one feels small, restricted, and poorly organized. Most of what you see are large tin sheets covering the sets, there is no access to the actual sets themselves. It felt like being shown billboards of what you could see, but never actually do.

The tour ends at Bollywood Park, which hosts a few staged performances. This was the only mildly enjoyable part. The on site restaurant is strictly vegetarian, which may not appeal to everyone, and the food was overpriced for its quality.

Overall, Mumbai Film City lacks substance, feels commercialized, and fails to deliver the behind the scenes magic one would expect. If you have been to Hyderabad's version, you will likely find this visit a complete letdown.

Film Studios: The Heart of Cinematic Magic

Film studios are the creative powerhouses that bring stories to life, turning scripts into immersive visual experiences. These spaces are more than just physical locations—they are hubs of imagination, where directors, actors, and technicians collaborate to craft films that captivate audiences worldwide. From grand soundstages to cutting-edge post-production facilities, film studios play a vital role in shaping the magic of cinema. Whether producing large-scale blockbusters or intimate indie films, these studios provide the foundation for storytelling at its finest, blending artistry with technical brilliance.

Yash Raj Films: A Legacy of Excellence in Indian Cinema

Yash Raj Films (YRF) stands as a pillar of Indian cinema, synonymous with grandeur, romance, and timeless storytelling. We spent in hour in the bus touring the Film city with only 2 stops. One was the famous temple that is reused in movies by changing Gods. They were getting it ready for a Shiva temple. That was interesting. Everything else was just drive by. Then they brought us to the "theme park" which had some interesting props and some shooting going on that we could watch. We saw Kadar Khan and few other actors. Then there was a very long (1-1/2 hr) live show which included dances by a SRK double. But we were basically made to watch rest of the mediocre show because the buses won't come to get you until the show is over. No one could ever tell us how long some activity is going to take which would have helped set expectations. The first 1 hour of actual tour is fun. Maybe 30 min in the theme park is sufficient. But rest of the 1-1/2 hrs of the talent show is just torture! Hardly anything was in English so we had to keep translating for our daughter who doesn't speak Hindi and also for several non Indians. All in all, kind of OK but could be better and more entertaining.

featured_reviews.name: Akash Kapoor
featured_reviews.review_text:
Just wanted to pass along our thoughts on the Bollywood tour as we felt our experience was a little disappointing to say the least for the City + Bollywood Tour.

Starting with the very beginning, the guide was late in the morning. We planned for 9-930 the night before, but he didn't arrive until 10:30am citing traffic as the reason. But as Indians we are all well aware that traffic is the norm in Mumbai and should be planned for accordingly.

A late start means everything was either delayed or rushed as a result. We proceeded with the tour and had to mention each of the viewpoints serving as a reminder whereas I would think it's an expectation that the guide would show us everything without mention. At Taj and Gateway of India we made a short stopover but were wondering that for us it turned out that we had already seen it before but for other tourists how would you expect them to see and enjoy the place in a short rushed time? We then reminded him of Mani Bhawan and other viewpoints, before making our way towards "star homes".

This was definitely the most oversold part of the tour as we saw Shahrukh Khan and Salman's house and Farhan Akhtar. In fact there were other houses on the way that we enquired about to which the guide informed us that it belonged to this celebrity etc, but again I would think this is an expectation, especially when your travellers are Indian. (no kidding, I was able to provide more celebrity addresses on an Ola cab ride) we asked of other houses in Pali Hill and Amitabh's house but it was "out of the way" and also apparently the houses you show depends on where the tour begins which is quite disappointing, a tour should have a proper itinerary.

After the fact, I also reconciled with the word doc and noticed the restaurant we were taken to was Shalimar and not Copperchimney - we were not given an option and once again, this speaks to my point that as the guest I felt like I should have policed the entire route and every fine detail (maybe I should have gotten paid to be the co-pilot). The restaurant was definitely not hygienic as there were fruit flies on pickles and even our drinks but since we were already "late" for the dance we made our way out to SJ. The studio itself is pretty substandard and for serials, yet the guide did a good job to show us around because he was kind enough to arrange us another viewing of another shoot at Filmistaan. At the same time, he emphasized that it was a personal favor though he mentioned the company has relations with studios so they are aware of shoots so not sure if the facts reconciled there and if it really was an additional favor. Such additional favors feel quite burdening so would try and watch the language for guests.

The highlights were the singing studio though again the experience should not feel rushed and feel as if it is not included in the tour but done as a favor. (The guide was kind to ask if any of us sings, but if we said no it would not be a part of the tour... I would expect the tour to be complete as per the itinerary because a traveller would not know what a recording studio experience is like regardless of whether or not they sing).It should be a more organized natural part of the tour as it changes the way one perceives the tour and enjoys it.

All in all, at over $200 per person the tour was not worth the price whatsoever. The car itself was substandard, I'm sure at that cost a newer fresher car can be arranged as it smelled of smoke (cigarette smokes) which is quite disgusting.
